meta.title: Muscle Keeper — protect your muscle during GLP-1 treatment
meta.description: Estimate your risk of losing muscle during treatment with Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and other GLP-1 medications, plus a suggested daily protein target.

hero.eyebrow: For people using Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro or other GLP-1 treatments
hero.title: You’re losing weight. The question is how much muscle you’re preserving.
hero.subtitle: Some of the weight lost during GLP-1 treatment may come from lean mass, not just fat. Answer 12 questions and get a personalised risk estimate.

problem.title: The muscle you lose doesn't come back on its own
problem.body: GLP-1 treatments can produce substantial weight loss. But total weight does not tell you how much came from fat and how much from lean mass. Without enough protein and muscle stimulus, you may reach a lower number on the scale without preserving all the muscle you need.

howItWorks.title: How it works
steps: Answer 12 questions about your treatment, progress, diet and current training.
We estimate your risk of muscle loss and a suggested daily protein target.
See your result immediately and receive a copy by email with the next steps.

landing.disclaimerNote: This is not a medical test and does not directly measure your body composition. It is a general estimate based on your answers.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about GLP-1 and muscle mass

items.question: Can GLP-1 treatments cause muscle loss?
items.answer: Some of the weight lost during GLP-1 treatment may come from lean mass, which includes muscle, water and other tissues. The proportion varies from person to person and cannot be measured accurately using a standard scale alone.

items.question: How can I tell whether I'm losing muscle mass?
items.answer: A standard scale cannot distinguish fat from lean mass. Body-composition tests can provide more information, while factors such as weight-loss rate, strength, physical activity and protein intake can help estimate risk.

items.question: How much protein do I need during GLP-1 treatment?
items.answer: It depends on your weight, age, activity, health and goal. Muscle Keeper provides a general reference, but a registered dietitian can tailor the amount to your individual situation.

items.question: Is walking enough to preserve muscle?
items.answer: Walking is beneficial for health, but it does not provide the same muscle stimulus as strength training. Preserving muscle during weight loss usually requires some form of strength work adapted to the person's ability.

items.question: What if I have nausea or low appetite?
items.answer: Nausea and low appetite can make it harder to eat enough protein and maintain a training routine. Do not change your medication on your own. If symptoms are severe or persistent, discuss them with the professional supervising your treatment.

result.title: Your personal estimate

interpretation.baix: Your answers show several factors that support muscle preservation, although strength and protein still deserve attention.
interpretation.mitja: Your answers indicate several factors that may increase lean mass loss during treatment.
interpretation.alt: Your answers combine several factors associated with a higher risk of lean mass loss. It is worth reviewing them with a professional soon.

result.factorsTitle: What is having the greatest impact on your result

factors.noCurrentTraining: You are not currently doing strength training.
factors.noBaselineTraining: You already had a low level of strength training before starting treatment.
factors.lowProteinMeals: You include a clear protein source in relatively few meals.
factors.fastWeightLoss: Your current rate of weight loss is high, which is associated with greater lean mass loss.
factors.longTreatment: You've been on treatment for several months, which increases your time of exposure to the risk.
factors.lowAppetite: Low appetite may make it harder to get enough protein.
factors.nauseaFatigue: Nausea or fatigue can make it harder to keep up training and eating well.
factors.ageRisk: Your age makes preserving muscle during weight loss especially important.

methodology.title: How we calculated this estimate
methodology.body: We combined your weight change, age, sex, time on treatment, strength activity, training availability and approximate protein intake. The result identifies risk patterns but does not directly measure your body composition.

cards.leanLossRatio: Estimated share of weight loss that may be lean mass
cards.projected6m: Estimated lean mass loss at 6 months if your current pattern continues

result.disclaimerBox: This result is a general estimate based on your answers and broad population patterns. It does not directly measure your body composition or constitute a clinical diagnosis. Discuss it with your doctor or registered dietitian before making significant changes.
result.ctaTitle: Losing weight should not mean giving up your muscle
result.ctaBody: We're building a strength and nutrition programme for people using GLP-1 treatments: realistic when you feel well and when you are dealing with low appetite, fatigue or nausea. We'll email you when it becomes available.

footer.disclaimer: Muscle Keeper provides general information and does not replace advice from your doctor, endocrinologist or registered dietitian. Do not change your medication or dose based on this app.

privacy.title: Privacy and health data
privacy.intro: Your answers about medication, symptoms, weight and habits may reveal information about your health and are considered special-category data under Article 9 of the GDPR. We process them only under the conditions explained below.

sections.title: Data controller identity
sections.body: This section is pending completion with the legal name, tax ID and registered address of the data controller before this app goes into production.

sections.title: Contact details
sections.body: For any privacy question or to exercise your rights, write to {contactEmail}.

sections.title: What we store
sections.body: We store your email, quiz answers, calculated result and the technical information required to provide the service. We do not sell this data or share it with third parties for advertising purposes.

sections.title: What we use it for
sections.body: We use this data to calculate and display your result. Only when you provide separate consent will we also use your email to send Muscle Keeper content and updates. We do not use your health data for personalised advertising.

sections.title: Legal basis
sections.body: We process your health data (medication and symptoms) based on your explicit, separate consent, which you can withdraw at any time. The technical data needed to provide the service is processed on the basis of performing the contractual relationship established when you use this tool.

sections.title: Where your data is stored
sections.body: Data is stored in Supabase, with the database configured in a European Union data centre. If we add other providers in the future (for example, for sending emails), we will add them to this list before switching them on.

sections.title: International transfers
sections.body: We do not currently transfer your personal data outside the European Economic Area. If this were to change, we would update this policy before doing so and, where required, ask for your consent.

sections.title: How long we keep your data
sections.body: Specific retention periods are still pending definition. Until they are published here, you can request deletion of your data at any time by writing to {contactEmail}.

sections.title: Automated decisions
sections.body: The result we calculate is an informational estimate, not an automated decision with legal or similarly significant effects on you. It is not used to accept or deny any service, or to make decisions about your medical treatment.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right to access your data, rectify it, request its erasure, restrict or object to its processing, and request portability. You can also withdraw your consent at any time and file a complaint with your country's data protection authority (in Spain, the AEPD) if you believe we have not handled your data correctly. You can exercise any of these rights by writing to {contactEmail}.
